newsitem.title: USA: Northfield Labs gets FDA nod for trials.
newsitem.headline: Northfield Labs gets FDA nod for trials.

text.p: Northfield Laboratories Inc said Wednesday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to conduct clinical trials of its blood substitute, PolyHeme, at a 10-unit level.
That level is equivalent to replacing the total blood volume of an adult human.
Previously, Northfield said it has infused patients with up to six units of PolyhHeme, which is equivalent to six units of blood.
Northfield said the expanded study will be conducted under Phase II testing protocols that the company has followed during the past year.

The company said about 80 percent of all blood transfusions are at the six-unit level or less. "The clinical trials at a higher dosage will allow the company to explore broader indications," Richard DeWoskin, chairman, said in a statement.
DeWoskin said Northfield also is seeking approval to conduct multi-site trials of PolyHeme under a Phase III testing protocols.

"While we cannot predict precisely when FDA clearance will be received for the Phase III trials, we are encouraged by the FDA's responses and will move expeditiously to obtain clearance and begin the final testing as quickly as possible," he added.
Steven Gould, Northfield president, added that he believes the medical community is receptive to PolyHeme as a potential transfusion option in trauma cases.
